claim.pdf_says: Increment index-name-1 (for a different table) or identifier-2   * (an asterisk beside the box, marking it optional)
claim.why_it_matters: The asterisk mark beside the last flowchart box became a level-3 markdown heading ('### \*') that splits the box label 'Increment index-name-1' in two and inserts a bogus heading into the document outline.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 810 (2014 p.786, Figure D.1): the last flowchart box reads 'Increment / index-name-1 / (for a different / table) / or identifier-2' with a lone '*' to its right, the footnote mark meaning the operation is optional. The markdown renders that box as 'Increment', then a level-3 heading '### \*', then 'index-name-1\ (for a different table) or identifier-2'. Both quotes are accurate. No text is lost (the asterisk and the whole label survive), so the meaning of the figure is recoverable, but the transcription injects a spurious heading into the document outline and splits the box label across it. That is a real structural transcription defect beyond wrapping; it has no normative effect (informative Annex D flowchart), so cosmetic is the right severity.
